acceptance: A journey test: a writer seat that creates a file outside its writable list ends with a verdict that is not PASS, and the signal names the path and the next step
A seat's input states its writable paths, or a directory grant for new files exists, with a test that a new file in that directory survives
An existing file outside the grant is still restored
fix: Design first. Two facts need a home. (1) The verdict of a writer seat must reflect the tree that remains: a fence removal of a path that the seat created is not PASS, and the signal names each path and the next step. (2) A brief needs a way to allow new files in a named directory without allowing edits to existing files there, or the seat must be told its writable list in its input, so that it can choose a permitted name or stop.

intake_override.reason: changes the worktree fence and the verdict of a writer seat, which the console-builder path depends on

summary: On 2026-11-05 a console-builder seat for B11 slice 1 created 4 new files whose names were not on its --writable list. The worktree fence removed them at the end of the dispatch, and logged a WARN. The run verdict stayed PASS, and the report said 212/212 tests pass. The tree that remained did not compile (commitgate.go: o.writeReviewRecord undefined). A caller that reads the verdict is told that broken work passed. The seat cannot know a new-file name in advance, and --writable refuses a directory, so this happens whenever a brief does not name each new file exactly.
title: A build seat's new files are erased by the fence, and the seat still reports PASS
